record_only.description: Title-level diagnostic framing was captured only as provenance and not used for ranking.
record_only.source_text_value: Acute mesenteric ischaemia due to superior mesenteric vein (SMV) thrombosis

record_only.description: A previous ED encounter and clinician differential diagnoses are narrative context, not rankable observations in this blind snapshot.
record_only.source_text_value: 3 days earlier with symptoms of mild abdominal discomfort with mild increase in inflammatory markers giving differential diagnosis of mild diverticulitis, colitis or possible urinary tract infection and discharged with antibiotic

record_only.description: Repeated labs described after the initial diagnostic workup are retained as early course severity context and excluded from ranking.
record_only.source_text_value: Repeated blood tests showed ... WCC was 23.7×10^9/L, CRP was 296 mg/L, serum creatinine level was 163 μmol/L, urea level reached 17.0 mmol/L, AST was 63 IU/L, albumin level was 27 g/L and ammonia level was 40 μmol/L

record_only.description: A suspected post-admission encephalopathy label is clinician interpretation and is not rankable.
record_only.source_text_value: After admission and 24 hours following diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischaemia secondary to SMV thrombosis, patient became confused and agitated, hepatic encephalopathy was suspected.

record_only.description: Medication and anticoagulation choices are treatment course, not diagnostic snapshot observations.
record_only.source_text_value: Intravenous antibiotic; co-amoxiclav 1.2 g Three times a day and anticoagulation; heparin infusion 5000 units loading dose followed by continuous intravenous infusion 18 unit/kg/hour were commenced as the initial conventional therapy.

record_only.description: Deterioration after diagnosis and the operative decision are course/treatment boundary facts.
record_only.source_text_value: patient started to develop sepsis and severe peritonitis 24 hours after diagnosis of mesenteric vein thrombosis, intestinal necrosis with impending perforation was suspected

record_only.description: Operative findings and procedures occurred after the diagnostic snapshot.
record_only.source_text_value: Resection of 120 cm of gangrenous small bowel segment 30 cm from duodenojejunal flexure followed by dissection of SMV and thrombo-embolectomy using fogarty catheter

record_only.description: ICU, ventilation, anticoagulation adjustment, relaparotomy, nutrition, discharge, and wound care are treatment/outcome course.
record_only.source_text_value: intensive care unit on mechanical ventilation with systemic heparinisation ... second laparotomy and bowel anastomosis ... enoxaparin ... warfarin ... discharged home

record_only.description: Postoperative pathology is not part of the blind diagnostic snapshot.
record_only.source_text_value: small bowel segment with mesenteric vascular thrombosis, ischaemic change in bowel, viable resection margins

record_only.description: Recovery and follow-up plans are late course and not rankable.
record_only.source_text_value: At 6 weeks postoperative, the patient was able to return back to his normal life ... thrombophilia screening ... now on warfarin tablets ... Rheumatology referral

record_only.description: Epidemiology, causal interpretation, and mortality framing from the discussion are not rankable case observations.
record_only.source_text_value: Mesenteric venous thrombosis ... accounts for 6%-9% of all the cases of acute mesenteric ischaemia ... mortality rate ... ranges from 20% to 50%

extraction_quality_notes: No target-label field or disease-suffixed observed axis was added.
Rankable observations were limited to presentation and diagnostic workup facts available around emergency surgical referral and CT imaging.

Temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, platelet count, coagulation studies, exact creatinine value at initial referral, and exact liver-function values were not provided in the diagnostic snapshot.
Repeated laboratory deterioration after the initial CT/workup was retained as record_only because the article presents it after the initial diagnostic snapshot.
disease_label_per_paper: Acute mesenteric ischemia from superior mesenteric venous thrombosis
